notes: Building setbacks are the permissible building zone shown on the Concept Plan.
Development must substantially comply with the Concept Plan, and a development plan approved by the Planning and Zoning Commission and the City Council is needed before any building or other permit.
The applicant must give the Town a traffic management plan for the Zoning Administrator's approval and follow it.
Development may be phased. Existing structures that do not match the Concept Plan may stay until their phase is built.

notes.heading: Parking
items: The property must always have at least 932 parking spaces.
The parking garage must be built before the building permit for the consolidated athletic center, with at least 1,024 spaces before that center's occupancy permit.
During construction the Zoning Administrator may approve a temporary parking plan that uses gravel lots and tandem parking.
Garage ramps may not be expressed on facades facing public streets or adjacent properties, and steel garages and steel guard cables are prohibited.

notes.heading: Exterior appearance
items: Masonry includes brick, stone, cultured stone, glazing and plate glass, three-coat stucco and split face concrete masonry units. A parking structure may use other cladding if the Town finds it compatible.
Accent materials such as stucco, metal paneling, tile and fiber cement siding are limited to 15% of each wall facing or visible from public streets and 40% of walls not visible from public areas.

Aluminum siding, fiberboard or Masonite siding, wood roof shingles and unfinished concrete block are prohibited as primary cladding. Wood shingles and composite shingles with less than a 50-year life are prohibited as roofing.
Glass must be clear or tinted, not reflective.

notes.heading: Athletic fields and lighting
items: Dugouts, bleachers, backstops and similar athletic structures may be moved anywhere within the building zone.
When the football field press box and bleachers are built, the field speakers move to the west side and face east.

Additional athletic lighting needs the Zoning Administrator's approval. If it is denied, the City Council may decide only after a public hearing held at least 10 days after notice to owners within 200 ft.
Tennis court lighting may not exceed 60 ft in height, must be shielded, and must be off by 10 p.m. Monday to Saturday and all day Sunday.
